title: Oil above $100 pins the rupee near 95.5 as the Sensex claws back in the closing auction
standfirst: A fourth day of the West Asia oil shock rippled through every Indian asset: bonds fell, the rupee hit a week low, and stocks only turned green in the last 15 minutes. Abroad, the ECB hiked and Fed hike bets firmed after hot US producer prices.

items.text: Sensex ended 138 points higher at 74,903 and the Nifty 46 points up at 23,478, snapping a three-session slide, but only after a 1,000-point swing during the closing auction on expiry day.
Brent crude climbed past $105 as US-Iran strikes escalated, up nearly 15% since the start of September. Oil is the single thread running through every move today.
The rupee fell 38 paise to close at 95.46 per dollar, its third straight day of losses, with state-run banks selling dollars on the RBI's behalf to slow the slide.
Government bonds weakened for a second day as US Treasury yields pushed toward 5%, their highest since 2023, and a global sovereign bond sell-off deepened.
Molbio Diagnostics hit a 20% upper circuit, now 87% above its IPO price, while NSE's selling shareholders may trim the size of the exchange's own IPO.

The RBI will run a 26-day reverse repo auction on Friday to pull ₹5 lakh crore out of the banking system, after using currency swaps to drain a $115 billion cash surplus. Liquidity is being tightened deliberately.
A Reuters poll expects August retail inflation at a 20-month high on food and fuel. The print lands early next week and will shape whether a rate hike enters the RBI's conversation.
SEBI chief Tuhin Kanta Pandey said the Closing Auction Session stays, but the way derivatives settlement prices are set on expiry days will be reworked.
SEBI and the RBI launched Demat 2.0, a pilot for tokenised corporate bonds settled in wholesale e-rupee; REC, L&T and IIFL have already raised ₹1,025 crore on it.
Merchandise exports grew over 15% between April and August, Piyush Goyal said, a rare cushion for the current account while the oil bill balloons.
The ECB raised rates to 2.50% and lifted both inflation and growth forecasts; Lagarde warned the energy-driven price shock will persist into 2027, with October 'in play' for another hike.
US producer prices rose more than expected on diesel costs, and traders now put a 70% chance on a Fed rate hike at the 16 September meeting. US CPI comes Friday.
Wall Street slipped for a third day, the Dow down 0.6% and the Nasdaq 0.9% on Wednesday, with chip stocks such as SK Hynix, AMD and Nvidia falling up to 6.5%.
Washington banned some Canadian alcohol, dairy and motorbike imports as the trade war with Ottawa escalated; copper eased after reports the White House is hesitating on its own tariff plan.

watch: Friday: RBI's ₹5 lakh crore 26-day VRRR auction; US CPI for August (the number that decides the Fed hike).
Early next week: India's August CPI, expected at a 20-month high.
16 September: Fed decision; Bank of Japan meets the same week and is expected to hike.
Brent above $105 and the 10-year Treasury near 5% are the two levels to keep on screen.
